# Rule-Change Integrity Checklist: Guaranteed Drop From Medium Fragments

**Purpose**: Requirements-quality validation for the amendment that changes the double-shot power-up drop rule (100% guaranteed for medium-fragment small asteroids, 10% retained otherwise). Tests how well the spec/plan/contracts *state* the rule change — not whether the code implements it.
**Created**: 2026-10-24
**Feature**: [spec.md](../spec.md) | [plan.md](../plan.md) | [contracts/guaranteed-drop-contract.md](../contracts/guaranteed-drop-contract.md)

**Note**: This custom checklist is generated by the `/speckit.checklist` command based on feature context and requirements.
**Review Ownership**: This checklist is a reviewer-owned requirements-quality review artifact. Mark an item `[x]` only when a reviewer has judged the corresponding requirements-quality criterion satisfied; `[x]` does NOT mean implementation work is complete.

## Supersession & Rate-Rule Consistency

- [ ] CHK001 - Does the spec state explicitly, in one place, that the 100% rule SUPERSEDES feature-003's FR-001 (rather than adding to or stacking with it), with a reader able to find no contradictory restatement of the old unconditional 10% rule elsewhere in the feature docs? [Consistency, Spec §Context, Spec §FR-001]
- [ ] CHK002 - Are the eligibility conditions for the guaranteed rate and the retained 10% rate stated as mutually exclusive and jointly exhaustive (every small asteroid falls into exactly one class) with no unclassified third case left open? [Completeness, Spec §FR-001, Spec §FR-003]
- [ ] CHK003 - Are "100% guaranteed" and "~1 in 10" quantified consistently everywhere they appear (spec Acceptance Scenarios, Success Criteria, plan, contract GD-4), with no paraphrase like "almost always" or "usually guaranteed" introduced in any document? [Clarity, Spec §SC-001, Spec §SC-003, Contract §3]
- [ ] CHK004 - Does the spec make clear that the retained 10% rule keeps feature-003's full semantics (independence, no memory/pity, same boundary convention) rather than the amendment silently implying a redefinition? [Consistency, Spec §FR-003, Spec §Assumptions]

## Origin Definition (Medium-Fragment Qualification)

- [ ] CHK005 - Is "product of the division of a medium asteroid" defined with precise birth-time and lifetime semantics (set once at birth, never mutated, never copied, absence marks non-fragments) such that no ambiguous reading like "ever had a medium ancestor via the large chain" or "currently near a medium" is possible? [Clarity, Spec §FR-004, Data-model §1]
- [ ] CHK006 - Is the two-generation chain case (large → two mediums → four smalls) explicitly resolved so a reviewer can verify the grandson smalls qualify because their immediate parent was a medium, without inferring it? [Completeness, Spec §Assumptions]
- [ ] CHK007 - Are the conditions under which a fragment LOSES its qualification specified (or a statement that it never does), covering border despawn, weapon suicides, and phase transitions? [Completeness, Spec §FR-004, Spec §Edge Cases]
- [ ] CHK008 - Is the tag's read-authority constrained in requirements (only one rule may branch on the origin), preventing future requirements from legitimately reusing the origin flag for unrelated balance rules without amendment? [Consistency, Data-model §4, Contract OF-3]

## Destruction-Cause Coverage

- [ ] CHK009 - Does the spec enumerate or explicitly generalize over every destruction cause that triggers the guarantee (projectile, asteroid-vs-asteroid collision, ship impact, and any mechanism added later), leaving no cause class to default silently to the 10% roll? [Completeness, Spec §FR-005, Contract GD-1]
- [ ] CHK010 - Is the destruction-vs-despawn boundary (border leaving produces NO drop) stated as a requirement rather than only as a game behaviour a reader must infer? [Clarity, Spec §FR-005, Spec §Edge Cases]
- [ ] CHK011 - Are results defined for the same-destruction-step overlap case: the two fragments co-destroyed by one event or by any simultaneous multi-cause event, ensuring the two-independent-drops rule covers coincidence, not only sequential destruction? [Coverage, Spec §FR-006, Contract GD-6]
- [ ] CHK012 - Are requirements defined for a fragment destroyed in the same step as its birth (e.g. ship overlapping the split point at death), where inheritance of position/direction must still hold despite the fragment never moving first? [Coverage, Gap]

## Inheritance & Downstream Semantics Integrity

- [ ] CHK013 - Is the requirement that a guaranteed drop is behaviourally IDENTICAL to a rolled drop (same spawn position/direction/speed rule, same collection, activation, no-stacking, despawn, non-interaction) stated so the amendment cannot be read as creating a distinct drop type? [Consistency, Spec §FR-002, Contract GD-2]
- [ ] CHK014 - Does the spec preserve feature-003's score/life neutrality programmatically (drops and their collections remain 0-score, 0-life-impact) with the change isolated to drop FREQUENCY only? [Consistency, Spec §FR-007, Spec §SC-005]
- [ ] CHK015 - Are requirements explicit that the 100% rule does not interact with, shorten, extend or stack the double-shot effect state (collection during an active effect remains consume-only)? [Consistency, Spec §Edge Cases, Contract §3 CR-3]
- [ ] CHK016 - Is compatibility with feature-002's sibling-fragment protection restated or referenced so the origin tag cannot be read as reintroducing fragment self-destruction or altering birthStep semantics? [Consistency, Spec §plan Constitution Check, Contract OF-4, RL-3]

## Measurability & Acceptance-Criteria Quality

- [ ] CHK017 - Can SC-001's "power-up appears after every single destruction — zero exceptions over any number of trials" be verified without implementation knowledge, and is the population (all destroyed medium-fragment smalls, all causes) bounded clearly enough for a reviewer to design the count? [Measurability, Spec §SC-001]
- [ ] CHK018 - Is SC-003's "clear majority produce no drop (roughly 1 in 10)" anchored to the same exact rate expression as feature-003 (independent per-event probability), so "majority" cannot be reinterpreted as any fixed percentage? [Clarity, Measurability, Spec §SC-003]
- [ ] CHK019 - Are the edge-case acceptance outcomes (two drops for two fragments, no drop for a border despawn) phrased as countable, position-verifiable outcomes rather than subjective adjectives? [Measurability, Spec §SC-004, Spec §Edge Cases]

## Dependencies, Assumptions & Traceability

- [ ] CHK020 - Is the dependency on feature-003 declared with a locatable mapping (which 003 clauses are inherited verbatim, which single clause is superseded), sufficient for a reviewer to review the amendment without re-reading the whole 003 spec? [Dependency, Spec §Context, Contracts README]
- [ ] CHK021 - Are the assumptions that remain silent-defaults (no visual marker for fragment origin, destruction cause irrelevance, terminal-state irrelevance) listed explicitly as assumptions — including a stated risk owner path if evidence later demands an exception? [Assumption, Spec §Assumptions]
- [ ] CHK022 - Is there a bidirectional traceability path between each FR (FR-001…FR-007) and its validation artifact (contract clause, data-model rule, quickstart scenario), with any FR lacking a mapped validation artifact flagged for the reviewer? [Traceability, Spec §FRs, Quickstart V1–V6, Contract §2–§4]
- [ ] CHK023 - Are the plan's regression locks (RL-1–RL-3) phrased so they read as reviewable requirements constraints (which files may change, which suites must hold), not as implementation instructions only a developer would parse? [Clarity, Contract §4, plan.md Project Structure]
